polka-dot.definition: A textile, clothing, or decorative design of evenly spaced round spots, usually matching in size and standing out against a solid background.

plaid.definition: A cloth having a crisscross design.

checkered.definition: Decorated with a regular pattern of alternating squares.

floral.definition: Decorated with a design based on flowers.

paisley.definition: A decorative pattern of curved teardrop-like motifs.

geometric.definition: Characterized by simple geometric forms in design and decoration.

abstract.definition: Art that uses shapes, colours, or forms instead of realistic subjects.

camouflage.definition: A pattern of colors and shapes intended to help something blend with its surroundings.

tie-dye.definition: A method of dyeing fabric after sections are tied, creating a mottled pattern.

herringbone.definition: A pattern of repeated broken zigzag lines resembling fish bones.

houndstooth.definition: A two-color textile pattern made of repeated broken checks with pointed shapes.
houndstooth.exampleUsage: The jacket uses a black-and-white houndstooth pattern.

argyle.definition: A pattern of overlapping diamond shapes, often crossed by thin diagonal lines.

tartan.definition: A pattern of crossing colored bands, traditionally associated with Scottish textiles.

gingham.definition: A woven cloth commonly showing small evenly sized checks.
gingham.exampleUsage: The tablecloth has a small blue-and-white gingham check.

pinstripe.definition: A very thin stripe repeated in a fabric or design.

chevron.definition: A repeated V-shaped line or pattern.
chevron.arabicTranslation: نقشة متعرجة على شكل حرف V

damask.definition: A patterned fabric with a design woven into its surface.

toile.definition: Here, a printed scenic pattern such as toile de Jouy; in clothing construction, the word can also mean a trial garment.
toile.exampleUsage: The curtain has a toile pattern showing a countryside scene.

ikat.definition: A textile pattern made by resist-dyeing threads before they are woven, often producing slightly blurred edges.
ikat.exampleUsage: The supplier identifies the cloth as ikat, made with threads dyed before weaving.

smooth.definition: Having a surface free from roughness or bumps or ridges or irregularities.

rough.definition: Having or caused by an irregular surface.

bumpy.definition: Having an uneven surface with raised bumps.

soft.definition: Easy to press or bend, and not hard to the touch.

hard.definition: Firm and difficult to press, bend, or cut.

fuzzy.definition: Covered with soft short fibers or fine hair.

silky.definition: Smooth and soft in a way that feels like silk.

grainy.definition: Having small visible or felt particles, or a texture resembling them.

matte.definition: Having a flat surface that does not shine or reflect much light.

glossy.definition: Having a shiny surface that reflects light.

polished.definition: Perfected or made shiny and smooth.

brushed.definition: Here, describing a metal finish with fine directional marks made by brushing.
brushed.exampleUsage: The brushed metal panel has fine parallel marks.

hammered.definition: Shaped or worked with a hammer and often showing hammer marks.

etched.definition: Cut, scratched or chemically formed into a surface to create a recessed design.

embossed.definition: Decorated with a raised design formed in or on the surface.

textured.definition: Having a surface with a noticeable pattern or feel.

ribbed.definition: Having parallel raised ridges on its surface.

woven.definition: Made or constructed by interlacing threads or strips of material or other elements into a whole.

knitted.definition: Made by intertwining threads in a series of connected loops rather than by weaving.

quilted.definition: Made of layers of fabric held together by patterned stitching.
